description: A lantern hung by the garden gate glowing just a shade warmer than its small flame could reasonably explain, casting a honey-colored circle of light on the moss below.
A single wildflower at the meadow's edge, barely taller than the others, its petals holding a soft luminescence that fades the moment you step closer to look.
Moonlight pooling in the hollow of an old oak's roots, still and bright, though the canopy above should have shadowed it entirely.
A firefly drifting low over the clover, its glow lingering a half-second longer than a blink — long enough to make you wonder if it was ever moving at all.
The pond's surface holding a faint shimmer in its very center, too steady and too deep to be a trick of the breeze, gone before you can point to it.
Something small and indistinct at the treeline — a shape between the ferns that seemed, for just a moment, to be watching before the shadows rearranged themselves into ordinary bark and leaves.
A fallen leaf resting on the stone path that seems, in the low afternoon light, to glow faintly amber from within rather than from above.
The farmhouse window casting a warm square of light onto the yard, the glow somehow reaching further than the room's single lamp should allow, as if the light itself is generous tonight.
A patch of clover near the hedgerow where the dew has not dried, though the rest of the field has been dry for hours, the droplets still catching the light like tiny held breaths.
Frost tracing along the windowpane in a pattern just shy of symmetrical — almost like something pressed a small, careful hand against the glass from the outside, then thought better of it.
A firefly pausing to glow, just a beat too long, on an outstretched fingertip.
A pond's still surface holding a faint, impossible shimmer beneath the lily pads.
A lantern hanging by the cottage door glowing just a shade warmer and softer than its small flame could rightly explain.
One wildflower at the meadow's edge standing slightly taller and more luminous than the rest, its petals holding a glow long after the sun has dipped below the hill.
Moonlight pooling in a hollow of the garden path that is entirely in shadow, still and silver, with nowhere obvious to have come from.
A shape at the very corner of the treeline, soft and small and almost the shape of something watching, gone entirely when you turn your head.
A single fallen leaf resting on the stream's surface, spinning slowly in a spot where the water is perfectly, inexplicably still.
The kitchen window fogging gently from within on a mild evening, a faint circular clearing in the mist just the size of a small pressed palm.
A robin perched on the fence post holding perfectly, unblinkingly still for a long quiet moment, its eye catching a light that isn't quite there.
An old stone wall with one patch of moss that stays a deeper, richer green than anything growing around it, even in dry weather, even in the grey of late afternoon.
